_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy P2, November 2024 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper2.pdf, paper2_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. Mathematical
Literacy questions hang off shared scenario boxes: the scenario (tables, graphs, plans and maps
described in bracketed words) is the 'context' of the first sub-question of each block and applies
to the sub-questions after it. memo_answer gives the guideline's working and final answer with
decimal commas kept; the guideline's mark codes (M method, A accuracy, CA consistent accuracy, RT
reading from table, C conclusion, O opinion, S simplification, R rounding) and level tags are left out.
FORMAT: 100 marks, 2 hours, four compulsory questions (Q1 20, Q2 20, Q3 34, Q4 26). ANNEXURE A (map
of Knysna) and ANNEXURE B (road map of Scranton) are in the separate addendum, tracked as
paper2_addendum.pdf; map-read answers come from the guideline.

questions.context: QUESTION 1 | 1.1 Zanele and Reneiloe are driving to Pretoria one morning. Zanele departs from Randburg and picks up Reneiloe who stays in Midrand. The car is driven at an average speed of 100 km/h from Randburg to Midrand and then to Pretoria. The clock below shows the time at which Zanele left Randburg. [Picture of a round wall clock with hands showing ten past ten.] [Source: www.googleimages.com]
questions.text: Identify the type of clock displayed above.
questions.topic: Measurement: conversions, time and estimating

questions.text: Write down the time Zanele left home in words.
questions.topic: Measurement: conversions, time and estimating
questions.memo_answer: Ten minutes past ten o'clock in the morning OR ten past ten in the morning OR ten past ten before noon

questions.text: Zanele arrived at Reneiloe’s place at 10:27. Determine how long it took her to get to Midrand.
questions.topic: Measurement: conversions, time and estimating

questions.context: 1.2 Sisanda drew the diagram below, showing the room she uses to study. [Floor plan of an L-shaped room: top wall 230 cm, right wall 200 cm, bottom wall 95 cm (with a window), inner step 88 cm, lower-left wall 135 cm (with the door), left wall 112 cm.]
questions.text: Define the term perimeter.
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs
questions.memo_answer: Perimeter is the distance around an object or shape.

questions.text: Hence, calculate the perimeter of the room in centimetres.
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs
questions.memo_answer:
Perimeter = 230 cm + 200 cm + 95 cm + 88 cm + 135 cm + 112 cm = 860 cm
(Accept (230 x 2) + (200 x 2) = 860 cm)

questions.context: 1.3 Timothy wants to lay ceramic tiles in his rectangular bedroom. Study the details of the size of the tiles that Timothy will use below. [Picture of a square tile measuring 43 cm by 43 cm.] [Adapted from www.googleimages.com]
questions.text: Convert 43 cm to metres (m).
questions.topic: Measurement: conversions, time and estimating

questions.text: Hence, calculate the area of the tile in m2. You may use the following formula: Area of a square = side × side
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs

questions.context: 1.4 Study the list of items below that are needed to assemble an office chair and answer the questions that follow. [Parts list: 1 casters x5; 2 base x1; 3 gas lift x1; 4 armrest x2; 5 seat cushion x1; 6 backrest x1; headrest x1; bolts and washers: 7 M8 x 22 mm for armrest, 8 M8 x 15 mm for backrest, 9 M5 x 18 mm for backrest; Allen key.]

questions.memo_answer:
M8 x 15 mm
M5 x 18 mm (accept any order)

questions.context: QUESTION 2 | 2.1 Knysna is a town in the Western Cape province of South Africa. The map of Knysna and surrounding areas in the Western Cape is shown in ANNEXURE A [street map of Knysna with the N2, Belvidere Village, Leisure Island, Paradise, Hornlee, Knysna Heights and Pezula Estate, number scale 1 : 56 000; in the addendum].
questions.text: Identify the national road on the map.
questions.topic: Maps: scales, street maps and directions

questions.text: In which general direction will you go if you travel from Belvidere Village to Leisure Island?
questions.topic: Maps: scales, street maps and directions

questions.text: The actual distance between Paradise and Hornlee is 7 km. Use the scale to calculate the map distance (to the nearest cm) between the two towns.
questions.topic: Maps: scales, street maps and directions

questions.context: 2.2 Busisiwe lives in Knysna Heights and plans a trip to Pezula Estate where she will spend the weekend with her friends. The distance between Knysna Heights and Pezula Estate is 11,2 km travelled via the N2. Busisiwe travels at an average speed of 100 km/h and she drives a Polo Vivo 1.4 with a fuel consumption of 5,7 litres per 100 km. Use the map of Knysna and the above information to answer the following questions.
questions.text: Calculate the approximate time, in minutes, that Busisiwe will take to travel from Knysna Heights to Pezula Estate. You may use the following formula: Speed = Distance ÷ Time
questions.topic: Maps: scales, street maps and directions
questions.memo_answer: Time = 11,2 km ÷ 100 km/h = 0,112 hours x 60 = 6,72 minutes (6 minutes 43,2 s; accept 7 minutes)

questions.text: Busisiwe and her friends travelled an approximate distance, in and around Pezula Estate, of 156 km with her car. Determine the total distance Busisiwe travelled during the weekend including her trip to Pezula Estate and back.
questions.topic: Maps: scales, street maps and directions
questions.memo_answer: Total distance = (11,2 km x 2) + 156 km = 178,4 km

questions.text: Busisiwe claims that she will spend less than R250,00 on petrol for her return trip including the weekend driving to and from Pezula Estate. Verify, with the necessary calculations, whether her statement is valid or not. NOTE: Cost of petrol = R24,45 per litre
questions.topic: Finance: financial documents, income and expenditure
questions.memo_answer:
Number of litres of petrol = 178,4 ÷ 100 x 5,7 = 10,1688 litres
Cost = R24,45 x 10,1688 = R248,63
Her statement is valid.

questions.context: QUESTION 3 | 3.1 Hein bought a fish tank at Premium Aquatics. The fish tank, with dimensions, is shown in the picture below. [Picture of a round glass fish bowl. Dimensions of the fish tank: radius = 2,1 foot.] [Source: https://aquapap.com/fish-tanks]
questions.text: Define the term volume in the context above.
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs
questions.memo_answer: Volume is the amount of space inside the fish tank.

questions.text: Calculate the height of the fish tank if the volume is 38,8 ft3. You may use the following formula: Volume of fish tank = π × radius2 × height, where π = 3,142
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs
questions.memo_answer:
38,8 ft³ = 3,142 x 2,1² x height = 13,85622 x height
Height = 38,8 ÷ 13,85622 = 2,8 foot

questions.text: The required temperature for the fish tank is 72 °F. Hein claims that he needs to set the temperature to 22,2 °C to be equivalent to the required temperature. Verify, with the necessary calculations, whether Hein's claim is valid or not. You may use the following formula: °C = (°F - 32°) x 5/9
questions.topic: Measurement: conversions, time and estimating

questions.text: The fish tank is 75% full of water. After adding stones to the bottom of the fish tank, the fish tank is 87% full of water. Calculate the volume of the stones in cubic feet (ft3). Round your final answer to ONE decimal place.
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs

questions.text: Hein has 7 fish in his fish tank: 3 yellow, 1 blue, 2 red, and 1 silver. Determine the probability (as a percentage) of selecting a silver fish from the fish tank.
questions.topic: Probability: simple and compound events

questions.context: 3.2 Hein wants to build a cabinet to display his fish tank and to prevent it from falling and breaking. His bricklayer informed him that he would need about 2 500 bricks for the cabinet he has in mind. Below is an image of the brick they will use. [Brick: length = 24 cm, width = 112 mm, height = 70 mm; weight of brick = 3,675 kg.]
questions.text: Calculate the total surface area (in mm2) of one of the bricks needed for the wall display cabinet. You may use the following formula: Total Surface Area = [2 (l × w) + 2 (l × h) + 2 (w × h)]
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs

questions.text: Determine the number of complete pallets transported by truck if one pallet contains 500 bricks.
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs

questions.text: The weight of the pallets transported is 9 187,5 kg. Convert the weight of one pallet to ton. NOTE: 1 000 kg = 1 ton
questions.topic: Measurement: conversions, time and estimating

questions.text: Hein claims that the volume of all the bricks is 4,7 m3. Verify, with the necessary calculations, whether Hein’s claim is valid or not. You may use the following formula: Volume of one brick = Length × Width × Height
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs

questions.text: One of the bricks that Hein is going to use costs R2,60 and the cost of delivery is R650. Calculate the cost Hein will have to pay for the bricks that will be needed, including delivery. Round your final answer to the nearest hundred rand.
questions.topic: Finance: financial documents, income and expenditure
questions.memo_answer: Total cost = R2,60 x 2 500 = R6 500 + R650 (delivery) = R7 150 ≈ R7 200

questions.context: QUESTION 4 | 4.1 Scranton is a hamlet in the town of Pennsylvania in New York, United States. Study the road map of Scranton in ANNEXURE B of the addendum [road map with a bar scale (12 miles), state and other roads, and places including Clarks Summit, Archbald and Blakely].
questions.text: List TWO types of scales used on maps.
questions.topic: Maps: scales, street maps and directions
questions.memo_answer:
Graphic / bar / linear scale
Ratio / numeric (number) scale

questions.text: Using the given scale, calculate the actual distance in miles between Clarks Summit and Archbald, if the distance on the map between these two places is 10,5 cm.
questions.topic: Maps: scales, street maps and directions
questions.memo_answer:
Scale bar = 6,7 cm = 12 miles
1 cm : 1,791044776 miles
Actual distance = 10,5 cm x 1,7910... = 18,80597015 ≈ 18,81 miles (accept 18,806 or 19 miles)

questions.text: A tourist must attend a conference in Blakely at 15:00. The travelling distance from his house to Blakely is 121,4 miles. He claims that if he leaves his house at 13:30 and stops at the petrol station for 25 minutes, he will be on time for his conference. The tourist travels at an average speed of 85 miles/hour. Verify, with the necessary calculations, whether his claim is valid or not. You may use the following formula: Time = Distance ÷ Speed
questions.topic: Maps: scales, street maps and directions
questions.memo_answer:
Time = 121,4 miles ÷ 85 miles/h = 1,4282... hours
0,4282... x 60 = 25,694... minutes; travel time = 1 h 25 min 42 s (1 h 26 min)
Arrival time = 13:30:00 + 01:25:42 + 00:25:00 = 15:20:42 (15:21)
His claim is invalid.

questions.text: Determine the probability of randomly selecting a road on the map that is a state road.
questions.topic: Probability: simple and compound events

questions.context: 4.2 Lwandile bought an Ugandan flag mounted on a rectangular wooden frame as shown in the diagrams below (diagram NOT drawn to scale). [Picture of the Ugandan flag: six horizontal stripes with a white circle in the centre. Dimensions of the rectangular wooden frame: length 22 inches, width unknown; circle diameter 9,5 cm.]
questions.text: Show that the area of the white cloth needed to cover the circle is 70,89 cm2. You may use the following formula: Area of a circle = π × radius2, where π = 3,142
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs

questions.text: Determine the width of the rectangular wooden frame in centimetres, if the area of the rectangular wooden frame, without the circle, is 2 682 cm2. You may use the following formula: Area of a rectangle = Length × Width NOTE: 1 inch = 2,54 cm
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs

questions.text: Lwandile claims that the width of ONE of the rectangular bars is 8 cm. Verify, with the necessary calculations, whether his claim is valid or not.
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs
questions.memo_answer:
Width of one bar = 48 ÷ 6 = 8 cm (OR 47,996 ÷ 6 = 7,9993... ≈ 8 cm)
Lwandile's claim is valid.
